verses.verse:
अंगुल्यपान्त भागेन छिद्राच्छादः प्रसंशितः।
नात्यग्रेण न मूलेन बंशी छिद्रान् प्रपेरयेत्।७९।
verses.text: Covering the holes with the part of the finger just short of its end is praised; one should not press on the flute's holes with the very tip or with the base [of the finger].

verses.verse:
ऋजुस्वराणामुच्वारे क्लिष्ताम् परिकल्पयन्।
श्रुतिस्पर्शधिया चैव स्थापये दंगुलीयकान्।८०।
verses.text: Foreseeing difficulty in sounding the ṛju (plain) notes, and with a mind to touching the śrutis, one should place the fingers [accordingly].

commentary.text: The practitioner should bear in mind that sometimes, to sound komal notes, even half a hole will have to be opened, and then it may be impossible to bend the finger. The second point is that if, in going from one note to another, touching the śrutis in between — that is, mīṇḍ (glide) — is wanted, then the placement of the fingers can be a hindrance. So, to be saved from troubles that will come in the future, place the fingers correctly right now. For this it is best to set the upāntya (next-to-last) part of the fingers on the holes. Some people bend the long finger for the convenience of the little finger. This is wholly harmful. For clarity, look at the figures.

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers
